findings.issue: Sizing defaults offer a 4 GiB Node container made safe by an L4 connection cap of about 2,500, assuming one in-flight unit per connection. Capacity planning, which replaces these starting points, says an L4 connection cap does not bound memory. It requires GOMEMLIMIT of at least M_flood, which includes 6,250 MiB of in-flight units on every Node.
findings.evidence: Deployment L493: "4 GiB (hypothesis) ... (a) Size for it, or (b) cap connections per Node at the L4 balancer near 2,500 (hypothesis; OQ-deployment-topologies-21)"; L521-522: "Connection cap (b) (3,686 MiB GOMEMLIMIT − 1,243 MiB budgets) / (592 KiB per connection + 320 KiB per in-flight unit) ≈ 2,700 → about 2,500 per Node"; L489: "Starting points; Capacity planning replaces them". Capacity L221: "80 connections can hold all 20,000 units (target): an L4 connection cap alone does not bound memory, and M_flood charges I_max × m_u, 6,250 MiB (hypothesis), on every Node"; L182: "GOMEMLIMIT ≥ max(M_node, M_flood)"; L387: "Independent limits below M_flood are not allowed".
findings.fix: Remove option (b) as a way to fit 4 GiB, or state that it holds only once OQ-capacity-planning-5 lowers the in-flight unit or HTTP/2 stream ceiling. Point Node container sizing to Capacity planning's GOMEMLIMIT ≥ max(M_node, M_flood) and keep 4 GiB only as an idle-connection figure.

findings.issue: The example Bundle's `support-chat` Route attaches both an `ai.token-budget` and an `ai.semantic-cache` Policy, and its Gateway has one State Store. Scalability forbids attaching `ai.semantic-cache` in a Cell whose State Store holds Token Budget keys until a second connection exists. The AI/LLM gateway's `support-chat` attaches no Semantic Cache, and Capacity planning repeats the MUST NOT.
findings.evidence: Configuration model L1169-1172: "policies: - name: apikey-partner ... - name: token-budget-partner - name: semantic-cache-support      # turns on the Semantic Cache for this Route"; L1026-1029: a single `stateStore` with `driver: redis`. Scalability L302: "Until then, a Cell whose State Store holds `ai.token-budget` keys MUST NOT attach `cache` or `ai.semantic-cache`". AI/LLM gateway L597: "`support-chat` attaches none". Capacity L314: "this State Store ... MUST NOT hold `cache` or `ai.semantic-cache` entries".
findings.fix: Remove `semantic-cache-support` from `support-chat`, or attach it to a Route in a Bundle without `ai.token-budget`. Note that combining the two waits for OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-3's second State Store connection. Keep `cache.semantic` on the AIModel, which is harmless without the Policy.

findings.issue: Traffic management bounds a key's healthy State Store calls at min(offered, N × ceiling) per window. Accepted ADR-0008, the decision record for this design, bounds them at min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling), a bucket's capacity plus its refill, and names the Traffic management figure as a needed correction.
findings.evidence: Traffic L227: "A key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, N × ceiling) times per window." ADR-0008 L85: "a key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) times per window (target), a bucket's capacity plus its refill"; L139: "Corrections: ... Traffic management's and Scalability's N × ceiling call bound is 2 × N × ceiling." ADR-0008 L120 (Confirmation): a change to per-request State Store calls or ceiling derivation MUST amend the ADR.
findings.fix: State the call bound as min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) per window (target), a full bucket plus one window's refill per Node. Keep pack 8.8's N × ceiling for fail-open admission separate.

findings.issue: Scalability repeats the min(offered, N_serving × ceiling) per-window State Store call bound that accepted ADR-0008 corrects to 2 × N × ceiling.

ADR-0008 L85: "at most min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) times per window (target), a bucket's capacity plus its refill"; L139: "Traffic management's and Scalability's N × ceiling call bound is 2 × N × ceiling."
findings.fix: Change the hot-key call bound to min(offered, 2 × N_serving × ceiling) per window (target), and recheck the 25% and 50% shard-share thresholds that depend on it.

findings.section: T4: Kubernetes with Helm, HPA and CRDs; T5 and T6: VMs with systemd and edge sites
findings.issue: The termination rules size the Kubernetes grace period and systemd TimeoutStopSec against the Drain deadline alone. The Zero-downtime document, which owns Drain timing, requires them to exceed the exit bound, the Drain deadline plus the 5 s flush, so values that pass these rules can kill the post-commit and telemetry flush.
findings.evidence: Deployment L186: "| Termination | `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` MUST exceed the preStop wait plus the Drain deadline |"; L265: "`systemctl stop` starts a Drain, so `TimeoutStopSec` MUST exceed the Drain deadline." Zero-downtime L236: "`terminationGracePeriodSeconds` MUST exceed the preStop wait plus the exit bound (Drain deadline plus flush), 45 s against 5 s plus 30 s (target), as `TimeoutStopSec` exceeds 30 s (target)."
findings.fix: Say "the preStop wait plus the exit bound (Drain deadline plus flush)" for T4, and "the exit bound, 30 s after SIGTERM (target)" for TimeoutStopSec, citing Drain timeline defaults.

findings.issue: Scalability requires terminationGracePeriodSeconds to exceed the preStop wait plus the drain deadline. The Zero-downtime owner requires it to exceed preStop plus the exit bound, which includes the flush.
findings.evidence: Scalability L162: "Kubernetes' `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, 30 s by default, MUST exceed the preStop wait plus the drain deadline (target)." Zero-downtime L236: "MUST exceed the preStop wait plus the exit bound (Drain deadline plus flush), 45 s against 5 s plus 30 s (target)".
findings.fix: Replace "the drain deadline" with "the exit bound (Drain deadline plus flush), 45 s by default in the chart (target)" and link Drain timeline defaults.

findings.issue: The rate-limiting row says "`EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback". That usually means an EVAL retry, which is a second round trip. Pack 8.7 rule 1, ADR-0008 and Traffic management all say `NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and never makes a second call. ADR-0008 records this row as needing a correction.
findings.evidence: Tech stack L69: "GCRA as one Lua `EVAL` through rueidis; server `TIME`; `EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback". ADR-0008 L51: "`NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and schedules a reload, never a second call (pack section 8.7 rule 1)"; L139: "Corrections: the Library catalog's "`NOSCRIPT` fallback" means the `failureMode` path above, never an `EVAL` retry". Traffic L216: "so no request makes a second round trip".
findings.fix: Reword to "`EVALSHA`; `NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and schedules an off-path `SCRIPT LOAD`, never an `EVAL` retry".

findings.section: Secrets and environment variables > Environment substitution
findings.issue: This sentence uses the glossary term Drift for file mode, where Ruralz Control does not run. Pack section 11 defines Drift as something Ruralz Control detects and reports. The sentence also calls a group of file-mode Nodes a "Cluster", but section 11 defines Cluster as a control-plane-only kind of enrolled Nodes. An operator would expect Drift reporting that file mode never provides.
findings.evidence: 02-configuration-model.md (Environment substitution): "A file-mode Cluster with more than one Node SHOULD load rendered Bundles or OCI Revisions; divergence shows as Drift." Pack section 11, Drift: "Any difference between the digest or `/config/dump` a Node reports and the Revision Ruralz Control assigned from Git; Ruralz Control reports it." Pack section 11, Cluster: "A control-plane-only kind: a set of enrolled Nodes in one Environment...". 04-control-plane-and-gitops.md (Drift detection): "Drift is any difference between the digest or `/config/dump` a Node reports and the Revision assigned from Git (pack 11), evaluated on every heartbeat aggregate." Heartbeats exist only on the Control Stream. 01-system-overview.md (Deployment modes), file-mode failure domain: "Every Node reading that source; no canary unless CI runs one". Pack 8.1, Rendered Bundle: "the form file-mode Nodes SHOULD load when more than one Node reads it".
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with wording of about the same length, for example: "When several file-mode Nodes read one source, they SHOULD load rendered Bundles or OCI Revisions; without Ruralz Control no Drift is reported, so compare Nodes' `/config/dump` with `ruralz bundle diff`." Leave the rest of the paragraph unchanged.

findings.section: Distributed state catalog > Distributed rate limits
findings.issue: This paragraph makes a normative MUST depend on a `ratelimit` field, `localOnly`, that the Configuration model does not define. The field is only option (c) of an open question owned by Traffic management and resilience, and that owner recommends a different option, (a). Pack section 3 and style guide section 5 forbid using undefined fields; proposals belong in Open questions. Other documents mark `localOnly` as proposed.
findings.evidence: 11-scalability (Distributed rate limits): "A key whose `requests` exceed 25% of one shard's calls, about 25,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use `localOnly` mode, option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1, alone or beside (a)". The Configuration model's fixed `ratelimit` config fields are "`key` (CEL), `limits[]` with `requests`, `window`". 09-traffic, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1: "(a) `config.perNodeCeiling`, `config.burst` (recommended); (b) a headroom multiplier; (c) `localOnly` mode". 03-capacity-planning: "`localOnly` is proposed (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (c), OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11)". 04-high-availability: "should be `localOnly` (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (c), proposed)". Pack section 3: "No document may invent any other field; proposals go to Open questions."
findings.fix: Reword without removing the bound. For example: "...SHOULD use `localOnly` mode once OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 adopts option (c) (proposed, OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11); until then it needs a declared per-Node ceiling, a split `config.key` or its own Cell". Mark the `localOnly` entries in the Cell and Cluster bottlenecks table and in CE-12 as "(proposed)".

findings.issue: The pack gives "Cluster" two meanings, and the documents follow both. Section 11 says a Cluster is a control-plane-only kind of enrolled Nodes. Section 2 calls it any "Group of Nodes with one config", and 8.13 defines a Cell as one Cluster plus its State Store. Taken literally, no Cell can exist before M2, since Control mode is Planned (M2), yet Scalability plans Cells from M1. Deployment topologies and Traffic management therefore call file-mode Node groups "Clusters", while System overview and High availability avoid the term. The canonical term's meaning in file mode is undefined.
findings.evidence: Pack section 11, Cluster: "A control-plane-only kind: a set of enrolled Nodes in one Environment that share one Revision and form one Rollout target." Cell: "one Cluster and the State Store it uses in one Region". 11-scalability: "single-Region Cells work from Planned (M1)" and "Per-Cell enforcement itself is Planned (M1)". 01-deployment-topologies Figure 2: `subgraph fm["T2: file-mode Cluster in one Cell"]`, caption "*Figure 2: T1 and a CI-fed T2 Cluster.*", and "**No mixed modes in one Cluster.** Moving from T2 to T3 replaces Nodes". 09-traffic (Decision path): "so large file-mode Clusters SHOULD run Control mode or size the State Store." In contrast, 01-system-overview (Deployment modes) gives the file-mode failure domain as "Every Node reading that source", and 04-high-availability FC-20 says "all Nodes of a file-mode source".
findings.fix: Settle this through an Open question in the owner, configuration-model, followed by a pack amendment. Either (a) extend the section 11 Cluster and Cell definitions, for example "in file mode, the Nodes that read one source form a Cluster with no `Cluster` resource, Enrollment or Rollout", and let 8.13 Cells cover them; or (b) keep Cluster Control-mode only, define a file-mode Cell as "the Nodes reading one source plus their State Store", and have Deployment topologies, Traffic management and the Configuration model replace "file-mode Cluster".

findings.section: Control Store and high availability; API summary
findings.issue: No operation removes a Raft voter. The HA and DR runbook and the Deployment topologies T4 procedure both require an `admin` to remove the old voter before a replacement replica joins. `/api/v1/replicas` supports only GET and POST, and no CLI verb removes a voter. The replica-replacement runbook step therefore cannot be executed, and the "(b) manual (current)" option of OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-2 has no mechanism behind it.
findings.evidence: HA L396: "2. To replace one voter after volume or zone loss, an `admin` removes the old voter (mechanism: OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-2), mints a join token at `/api/v1/replicas`, and the new host runs `ruralz control join` then `ruralz control serve`". HA OQ-2: "how is a voter replaced after volume or zone loss, as `/api/v1/replicas` removes none ... (b) manual (current) | control-plane-and-gitops | Yes, for the Planned (M2) chart". CLI REST table: "| `/api/v1/replicas` | GET, POST | Replica health; one-time join token | `admin` |". Deployment topologies T4: "once an `admin` removes its old voter (OQ-deployment-topologies-20), then runs `join`".
findings.fix: Define voter removal in Control Store and high availability and in the API summary: `DELETE /api/v1/replicas/{serverId}` (`admin`, step-up TOTP, audited). Only the leader performs it, as a Raft `RemoveServer`, and it is refused when it would remove the leader or break quorum. Add a Ruralz Console Settings action. Have CLI and API surface mirror the row, optionally with a `ruralz control` verb. HA OQ-2 then only decides who calls it.

findings.issue: The complete example Bundle attaches both `ai.token-budget` and `ai.semantic-cache` to the `support-chat` Route, and the Bundle's single Gateway `stateStore` serves every Route. The example is the golden-corpus reference that readers copy, so it teaches a configuration that a MUST NOT rule prohibits.

findings.issue: The example Bundle's geo-block Plugin grants only request.headers.read and log.write. Under Plugin ABI v1 a Plugin can reject a request only by calling response_send, which needs response.send. Two documents give different Capability sets for one artifact, and the Configuration model's version, which is in the golden corpus, cannot deny a country.
findings.evidence: 02-configuration-model.md example Bundle: `phases: [onRequestHeaders]` / `capabilities: [request.headers.read, log.write]   # nothing else is granted` for `image: ghcr.io/acme/ruralz-plugins/geo-block:1.4.0@sha256:fc37c2971bb6...`. findings.section: CLI command tree > Test case format
findings.issue: The ruralz.test.v1 example targets the Configuration model's orders-summary Route, but its second case would fail against that Bundle. orders-summary authenticates through the inherited Gateway auth.jwt Policy jwt-default, and its authz-orders rule reads auth.claims.scope, so an x-api-key header alone gets 401. The aggregate response also nests each step body under its `group` key (order, stock), so a top-level `id` subset match cannot pass.
findings.evidence: 01-cli-and-api-surface.md: `- name: serves a partner key` ... `path: /v1/orders/42/summary` ... `x-api-key: {file: ./secrets/partner-key}` ... `expect:` `status: 200` `json:` `id: "42"`. 02-configuration-model.md: Route orders-summary attaches `cors-partner`, `authz-orders`, `ratelimit-orders`. The worked example says "`jwt-default` | Gateway | Slot `auth`; no Route auth Policy, so inherited". authz-orders: `rule: 'auth.claims.scope.split(" ").exists(s, s == "orders:read")'`. Steps: `group: order` / `group: stock`, where `group` is the "key under which the body is merged". apikey-partner is attached only on support-chat.
findings.fix: Send a JWT with the orders:read scope (for example `authorization: {file: ./secrets/partner-jwt}`) and expect `json: {order: {id: "42"}}`. Alternatively, point the API-key case at a Route that attaches apikey-partner.

findings.section: Go plugins to built-in Filters or WASM Plugins
findings.issue: The text introduces the tenant-guard Plugin as the way to handle logic that outgrows CEL, such as a signature check over the body. The Plugin declares only onRequestHeaders and no request.body.read or crypto.use, so it cannot read or verify a body. It is also scaffolded with the Go PDK (step 1), whose scaffold grants WASI clock.read and random.read. Neither is in spec.capabilities, so the derived imports would not be a subset and the Plugin would fail activation (RZ-CFG-028).
findings.evidence: 03-migration-from-krakend.md: "When the logic outgrows CEL, for example a signature check over the body, the same behavior becomes a WASM Plugin:" followed by `phases: [onRequestHeaders]` / `capabilities: [request.headers.read, request.headers.write, response.send, log.write]`. Step 1: "`ruralz plugin init tenant-guard --language go` creates a Go PDK project". 05-wasm-plugin-system.md: "`request_body_read` | `(offset i64, o, c)` | `request.body.read` | `onRequestBody`"; SDK matrix, Go / TinyGo: "Scaffold grants WASI's `clock.read`, `random.read`, `log.write`"; Contract: "Requested Capabilities | Derived from imports; a subset of `spec.capabilities`".
findings.fix: Add clock.read and random.read to tenant-guard's capabilities for the Go PDK. Then either reword the lead-in so it does not claim a body signature check, or add onRequestBody to phases and request.body.read and crypto.use to capabilities.
